column2: The king's settled house and the Lord's giving possession away from surrounding enemies retain the selected inheritance verb rather than prematurely substituting the rest wording of verse 11.
Look now represents the presentative, contrasting David's cedar house with God's ark inside the tent.
Nathan's advice encompasses what is in David's heart and explicitly rests on the Lord being with him; it is distinguished from the later nocturnal word.
That night's word comes to Nathan, whose commissioned report follows; no direct speech to David is inserted here.
The selected negative statement You will not build Me a house remains rather than an unmarked positive question; God addresses David with ordinary you.
The explanatory for, no house since the exodus and ongoing movement in lodging and tent remain, including both shelter terms.
The question retains one of Israel's tribes commissioned to shepherd and the nested question about a cedar house.
column3: The tribe antecedent and singular relative alongside collective addressees remain; judges is not substituted for the selected tribe word.

column2: Nathan receives a renewed instruction to address David; the Lord Almighty recalls the sheepfold and appointment over His people Israel.
Presence wherever David went, destruction of all enemies and established renown comparable to earth's great retain the three past actions.
Future place, planting, independent dwelling, no further anxiety and no renewed humiliation preserve the linked promises and their negative scope.
The judges-period clause continues verse 10 before rest from enemies and the selected statement that David will build Him a house.
column3: This you will build Him wording is not harmonized with verse 5, the son's building in 13 or I will build you in 27; its textual and interpretive relationships remain open.

column2: Fulfilled days, sleeping with ancestors, subsequent seed from David's body and prepared kingdom remain; the masculine relative is not made an unambiguous collective of all descendants.
He builds a house for God's name and God establishes his throne for ever; divine and human agency remain separate.
Father/son relation and the conditional coming of wrongdoing retain correction by human rod and afflictions, without converting the conditional to an accusation already fulfilled.
Mercy will not be withdrawn as from those removed before God; the selected plural those remains, without replacing it with Saul's name.
His house, kingdom and throne remain third-person and before Me remains divine first-person; no your/before you reading is imported.
Nathan reports according to all the words and all the vision; the completeness is the narrator's statement, not a claim of apparatus verification.
David enters and sits before the Lord, asking about himself and his house; loved me and repeated my Lord, Lord retain the selected wording and direct divine Thou.
The smallness comparison, servant's house far ahead and law of the human being remain with divine Thee/Thy.
column3: The law clause and its discourse force are unresolved; charter for humanity or an extraordinary-man reading is not silently substituted.

column2: David names himself in the third person in his question, then addresses divine Thou, retaining the Lord's knowledge of His servant.
Because of Thy word and according to Thy heart retain the two grounds, repeated action and greatness disclosed to the servant.
The continuation expresses divine magnification, none like Thee and no God besides Thee, with the community's heard-with-ears testimony.
column3: The infinitive's exact logical attachment remains provisional; the English passive magnification construes God as its object, not an omitted human achievement.

column2: Israel's uniqueness, God's leading and redeeming a people, name, greatness, manifestation, expulsion of nations and dwellings, and exodus remain in the full sequence.
column3: Third-person Himself shifts to direct Thee/Thy with the Greek's pronoun change. The linked infinitives and agency remain difficult; dwellings is not replaced with gods, nor is a second nation silently added.

column2: God prepares Israel as His people for ever and becomes their God; the prayer retains direct Thou and Thyself.
The request confirms the word about the servant and his house for ever, names Lord Almighty, God of Israel and continues as Thou hast spoken into verse 26.
The short selected unit contains only the wish for the name's everlasting magnification; no longer royal-house formula is supplied.
Revealing to the servant's ear, the nested I will build you a house, and finding heart to pray remain; quotation addresses David as you while David addresses God as Thee.
Thou art God, future words will be true and spoken good things for the servant remain distinct temporal claims.
Begin and bless, lasting presence before Thee, the explanatory divine speaker and future blessing from Thy blessing remain, closing the prayer.
Striking and routing foreigners precede taking the separated territory from their hand.
column3: Territory supplies a noun for the feminine substantivized participle; the place or object's exact identification remains open, and no Metheg-ammah replacement is made.

column2: Ground placement and cord measurement retain two lengths for death and two kept alive, followed by Moab's service and gifts.
column3: The selected equal pair of measured lengths is not changed to a two-to-one ratio, and no estimated number of people is supplied.

column2: Hadadezer son of Raab of Zobah and the Euphrates remain; establish his control interprets the hand idiom.
column3: The going participle's subject can be disputed; inherited he remains without an added name to settle the itinerary.

column2: One thousand chariots, seven thousand horsemen and twenty thousand infantry remain; disabled chariots and the hundred left retain the selected grammatical object.
column3: No horses are inserted as the explicit disabled object or a different cavalry total substituted.

column2: Damascus Syria's aid and David's striking twenty-two thousand Syrian men retain source, allegiance and count.
The Damascus garrison, Syrian service and gifts remain; gave victory is the inherited military-context rendering of the Lord's saving David wherever he went.
Gold armlets are taken to Jerusalem, and the full later notice about Shishak under Rehoboam son of Solomon remains.
column3: The retrospective historical notice is not removed to smooth chronology or converted to a prediction voiced by David.

column2: Masbak and selected cities remain with much bronze and the full Solomon notice listing sea, pillars, basins and vessels.
column3: The relationship between singular Masbak and the following plural cities is not repaired by supplying a second place-name.

column2: Toi of Hamath hears of the defeat of all Hadadezer's force; the sentence continues into his diplomatic response.
Ieddouran, peace inquiry, blessing for victory, opposition to Hadadezer and silver/gold/bronze vessels remain.
column3: The pronouns shift among Toi, his son and David; the opponent clause and final bearer remain contextually construed rather than supplied with a newly certain name.

column2: David dedicates these gifts together with silver and gold from all dominated cities; nations is not substituted for cities.
Idumea, Moab, Ammon, foreigners, Amalek and Hadadezer's spoil remain the complete continuation list.
David's renown and returning victory retain Idumea, Gaimale and eighteen thousand; the selected named region is not changed to Syria.
The garrison throughout Idumea, all Idumeans serving the king and repeated saving/victory notice remain.
David's kingship over Israel and ongoing judgment and righteousness for all his people retain the ethical pair and collective scope.
Joab's army responsibility and Jehoshaphat son of Ahia over records remain with the selected parentage.
Zadok son of Ahitub and Ahimelech son of Abiathar remain priests, with Asa as scribe; the father/son sequence is not reversed to match another passage.
Benaiah son of Jehoiada as counselor, the Cherethite/Pelethite coordination and David's sons as palace officials remain.
column3: The guard clause lacks an expressed office or governing preposition; no commander over is silently added. Plural group names interpret the singular collective labels, and palace officials is not changed to priests.
